subject: Assigning boundary values in the data block for vectors

messages.author: f383ad53e3901131
messages.subject: Assigning boundary values in the data block for vectors
parts:
Hi, I am new to STAN and have started learning by converting models coded in BUGS/JAGS to STAN, so that I could compare the results.

I was working on a statin example that my lecturer showed in class in JAGS, but had errors trying to compile the model in RSTAN. I have included the relevant sections of the lecture notes in the attached Word Document and also included the details from sessionInfo() in R. The error obtained was 

"TRANSLATING MODEL 'statin' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
COMPILING THE C++ CODE FOR MODEL 'statin' NOW.
Error : Invalid value of xs: model4bc3f773a0a_statin_namespace::model4bc3f773a0a_statin(i): xs[k0__] is 77, but must be less than or equal to 75"
failed to create the sampler; sampling not done


The model I used is as below:

data {
int <lower=0> study; // number of studies included
int<lower=0> ns[study]; // number at risk in statin group
int<lower=0> np[study]; // number at risk in placebo group
int<lower=0,upper=ns[study]> xs[study]; // number of deaths in statin group
int<lower=0,upper=np[study]> xp[study]; // number of deaths in placebo group
}

parameters {

real mu;
real gamma;
real sigma;
real beta[study];

}

transformed parameters {
real<lower=0> sigmasq;
real<lower=0,upper=1> ps[study]; // estimated risk in statin group
real<lower=0,upper=1> pp[study]; // estimated risk in placebo group

sigmasq<-sigma*sigma;

for (i in 1:study)
{
ps[i] <- inv_logit(beta[i]);
pp[i] <- inv_logit(gamma + beta[i]);
}
}

model {
for (i in 1:study)
{
beta[i] ~ normal(mu,sigmasq);
xs[i] ~ binomial(ns[i],ps[i]);
xp[i] ~ binomial(np[i],pp[i]);
}

mu ~ normal(0,10000);
gamma ~ normal(0,10000);
sigma ~ uniform(0,100);
}


The code i used to run the model was

data<-read.csv("statin.csv",header=TRUE)
dataset=list(xs=data$xs,ns=data$ns,xp=data$xp,np=data$np,study=9)
fit <- stan(file = "statin.stan", data = dataset, iter = 1000, chains = 4)


It seems that the boundary I declared in the data block for xs was the last value of ns (ie. 75). When i replaced 77 (xs[2]) with a value smaller than 75, the next error flagged was xs[4] as its value was greater than 75. The same issues were observed for xp. If i wanted to ensure that each xs/xp was less than or equal to ns/np, would I then have to create a for loop in the data block to ensure correct assignment of the boundary values? Would appreciate any advice on the syntax to resolve the issue.

Many thanks!

Kind regards,
Cindy

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Assigning boundary values in the data block for vectors
parts:
Hi, the normal model in Stan is parameterized as normal(mean,sd), not normal(mean,variance).  Also, sigma should be constrained to be positive, and you should use soft, not hard priors (that is don’t use a uniform prior on sigma).  Finally, your priors on mu and gamma are probably too weak.

Also, no, I don’t think you can use those wacky bounds for the xs and xp parameters.  But, really, any such bounds in the data statements are just for convenience.  There’s no need for you to include them in your model.
A

Dear Prof Gelman,

Many thanks for pointing out the errors and the suggestions!

As I had mistakenly thought that the normal model in STAN was normal(mean, variance), thus the priors for mu and gamma were specified too weakly. Using normal(0,100) for mu and gamma would probably be much better? For sigma, would using inv_gamma(0.001, 0.001) be better, please?

I was wondering if there would be cases which require boundaries for each element of a vector for a particular parameter? In this case, boundaries were not required as a binomial model was used, and the upper bound was naturally ns/np. Íf boundaries were required, how then should the syntax be specified, please?

Many thanks!

Kind regards,
Cindy

parts:
It depends on the scaling of your model, but I’d generally suggest priors such as normal(0,10) or even normal(0,1).  For sigma, maybe something like normal(0,10) (implicialty constrained to be postivie) would work.  Again, that depends on the scale of the parameters in your model.

Regarding bounds, these are only needed on parameters, not on data.

I was working on a statin example that my lecturer showed in class in JAGS, but had errors trying to compile the model in RSTAN. I have included the relevant sections of the lecture notes in the attached Word Document and also included the details from sessionInfo() in R. The error obtained was 

"TRANSLATING MODEL 'statin' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
COMPILING THE C++ CODE FOR MODEL 'statin' NOW.
Error : Invalid value of xs: model4bc3f773a0a_statin_namespace::model4bc3f773a0a_statin(i): xs[k0__] is 77, but must be less than or equal to 75"
failed to create the sampler; sampling not done


The model I used is as below:

data {
int <lower=0> study; // number of studies included
int<lower=0> ns[study]; // number at risk in statin group
int<lower=0> np[study]; // number at risk in placebo group
int<lower=0,upper=ns[study]> xs[study]; // number of deaths in statin group
int<lower=0,upper=np[study]> xp[study]; // number of deaths in placebo group
}

parameters {

real mu;
real gamma;
real sigma;
real beta[study];

}

transformed parameters {
real<lower=0> sigmasq;
real<lower=0,upper=1> ps[study]; // estimated risk in statin group
real<lower=0,upper=1> pp[study]; // estimated risk in placebo group

sigmasq<-sigma*sigma;

for (i in 1:study)
{
ps[i] <- inv_logit(beta[i]);
pp[i] <- inv_logit(gamma + beta[i]);
}
}

model {
for (i in 1:study)
{
beta[i] ~ normal(mu,sigmasq);
xs[i] ~ binomial(ns[i],ps[i]);
xp[i] ~ binomial(np[i],pp[i]);
}

mu ~ normal(0,10000);
gamma ~ normal(0,10000);
sigma ~ uniform(0,100);
}


The code i used to run the model was

data<-read.csv("statin.csv",header=TRUE)
dataset=list(xs=data$xs,ns=data$ns,xp=data$xp,np=data$np,study=9)
fit <- stan(file = "statin.stan", data = dataset, iter = 1000, chains = 4)


It seems that the boundary I declared in the data block for xs was the last value of ns (ie. 75). When i replaced 77 (xs[2]) with a value smaller than 75, the next error flagged was xs[4] as its value was greater than 75. The same issues were observed for xp. If i wanted to ensure that each xs/xp was less than or equal to ns/np, would I then have to create a for loop in the data block to ensure correct assignment of the boundary values? Would appreciate any advice on the syntax to resolve the issue.

Many thanks!

Kind regards,
Cindy

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Assigning boundary values in the data block for vectors
parts:
The bounds on data are there for error checking and
to help readers of the code understand what you have
in mind for data. They don't change the fit.

But failing early with a sensible error message is
what you want code to do, so we strongly recommend using
constraints on data wherever possible.

- Bob
